article_content: At least 12 people, mostly women, were killed and 47 others wounded in Mogadishu after Islamists and African Union forces exchanged shells on Thursday, according to an ambulance service official. 'I can confirm that at least 12 people died in today's fighting and we have collected 47 others who were wounded,' said Ali Musa, director of an ambulance service, speaking to CNN from Mogadishu. 'At one site, a shell landed on women selling milk, resulting in several casualties.' The shelling began in the morning when Islamist rebels fired mortars at Somalia's parliament building, where lawmakers were in session.

article_content: In the village of Sandvoort, Guyana, a community library has been established through the collaborative efforts of the villagers and Peace Corps volunteer, Matt Cusimano. The library was built with a budget of $5,000, with the community contributing nearly 30% of the costs through donated labor and space. Students in Sandvoort are significantly behind their expected reading level, but the library, stocked with over 3,600 books, is set to improve this. The library features three new computers, introducing villagers to digital literacy. For 9-year-old Kayla Hope, the library provides access to fairy tales like 'Cinderella', fueling her imagination and reading skills.

article_content: Apps have transformed how we communicate, travel, and use our time on the road. Tom Dunmore, creative director at Mediablaze, notes that apps are 'the next stage of the internet' due to their location sensitivity, ease of use, and constant connectivity. They are increasingly replacing traditional tools like maps and guidebooks. Paul English of Kayak found that users rely on their mobile phones for travel planning, similar to how they use computers. The travel app sector is booming, with Kayak dedicating 20% of its engineering team to app development. The app economy is significant, with substantial investment in app development. Realmac Software's 'Clear' app has been successful, selling over half a million copies. The barrier to becoming an app developer is lower than ever, with individuals able to publish apps alongside major brands.

article_content: Molly Conley, a top student and star lacrosse player at Blanchet High School in Seattle, was tragically killed in a random drive-by shooting on Saturday night. She was walking with friends along a residential road in Lake Stevens, Washington, celebrating her 15th birthday, when gunfire erupted, fatally hitting her in the neck. Molly had just turned 15 on Friday and was planning to spend the night at a friend's house before attending her birthday party on Sunday. Instead, her friends attended a vigil for her on Sunday at a local church, where over 800 people gathered to pay their respects. The police are investigating the incident, searching for a black SUV seen in the area, and exploring possible connections to other drive-by shootings in the vicinity.

Dahlan's associates have faced attacks from Hamas amid escalating tensions between the militant group and Fatah.

article_content: Alejandro Valverde claimed victory in stage 17 of the Tour de France, while Bradley Wiggins took a step closer to Britain's first overall victory. With three stages left, Wiggins leads teammate Chris Froome by just over two minutes. Valverde finished 18 seconds ahead of Wiggins and Froome, securing Team Movistar's first win of the Tour. The Spanish rider had a 2:35 lead at the start of the final 15-kilometer climb but struggled to maintain it as the British duo closed in. 'I gave it my all to resist their chase,' Valverde said after finishing first on the 143.5 km route. Valverde faced bad luck throughout the Tour, including three crashes in two days, but secured a stage win. Wiggins, wearing the yellow jersey for most of the race, is on the verge of becoming Britain's first Tour de France winner.

article_content: Washington (CNN) -- President Barack Obama announced on Thursday that he's sending up to 300 military advisers to Iraq. These advisers will help train and support Iraqi forces against the militant group, the Islamic State of Iraq and Syria (ISIS), which has taken several cities in northern and western Iraq. The advisers will also gather intelligence on ISIS and could assist in calling in airstrikes if authorized. One aircraft carrier and five warships are already positioned in the Persian Gulf. U.S. drones are flying intelligence missions over Iraq, and military sources tell CNN that a list of ISIS targets has been compiled. Obama stated that such action is necessary to prevent a civil war in Iraq that could destabilize the region and create a terrorist safe haven.

article_content: In August 2013, brothers Connor and Noah Barthe, aged 6 and 4, died after being strangled by a 100-pound snake that fell through the ceiling while they were sleeping at Jean-Claude Savoie's home. Savoie's home was above his exotic pet store, 'Reptile Ocean', in Campbellton, New Brunswick, Canada. The snake, an African rock python, was kept in a glass enclosure similar to an aquarium but managed to slither into the ventilation system and eventually fell into the living room where the boys were sleeping. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police announced the arrest of Jean-Claude Savoie 18 months after the incident. Leslie Matchim, Savoie's attorney, confirmed the arrest and stated that it remains to be seen if charges will be filed.

article_content: By Naomi Greenaway and Ruth Styles. Lou Street, a 39-year-old mother of four from Gravesend, appears carefree at first glance. However, she is suffering from motor neurone disease. She plans to spend her remaining time with her husband, John, and their two youngest children, Ria and Mimi. Lou has been open with her family, including her older children from a previous relationship. Ria, aged nine, is struggling to cope with the news. Lou has planned her funeral, which will include a celebration of her life led by a celebrant. She is concerned about her family's future, especially her young daughters' well-being and the potential need for a step-mother.

article_content: It's been over a century since Istanbul's residents were kept awake at night by tens of thousands of stray dogs howling. The dogs were rounded up and shipped to a deserted island in the Marmara Sea, where they starved to death, as part of a government effort to modernize Istanbul. Activists are protesting a proposed law to create 'natural habitat parks' for stray cats and dogs, calling them 'concentration camps.' article_content: Qantas has re-routed its London to Dubai flights to avoid Iraqi airspace due to rising tensions in the Middle East. This change, effective Thursday night, is a precautionary measure to avoid another MH17-like disaster. The new route, flying over Iran instead of Iraq, will add up to 10 minutes to the seven-hour journey. Qantas closely monitors flight paths over conflict zones, particularly after the MH17 tragedy, which claimed 298 lives, including 38 Australians. The airline's decision follows the US Federal Aviation Administration's increase of the minimum altitude for commercial flights over Iraq from 20,000 to 30,000 feet. Qantas' flights previously travelled over Iraq at altitudes of 38,000 to 41,000 feet. 'Safety is our first priority,' said a Qantas spokesman, adding that the rerouting is a temporary measure until further information becomes available.

article_content: Canadian authorities are investigating an incident involving Air Canada Flight 001, a Boeing 777 aircraft with 318 passengers and 16 crew members on board, which departed from Toronto's Pearson International Airport en route to Tokyo's Narita Airport on Monday. After an engine failure shortly following takeoff, the crew adhered to standard protocols by requesting an emergency landing and returning to Toronto. The aircraft landed safely at 3:53 p.m., but earlier, around 2:30 p.m., reports surfaced of debris falling from the plane, resulting in damage to several vehicles in the regional municipality of Peel. Eyewitnesses recounted hearing a loud noise and observing smoke, with the scene littered by pieces of gray, heavy material. Fortunately, no injuries were reported among the passengers or individuals on the ground. A comprehensive investigation into the incident is being conducted by Air Canada and Transport Canada.

article_content: Although you use it daily, here are some interesting facts you may not know about deodorant. Actor Matthew McConaughey reportedly doesn't wear deodorant. 1. Be thankful for your strong body odor. According to anthropologist Louis Leakey, it might have helped early humans survive. 2. The ancient Egyptians pioneered deodorants by applying scents to armpits using cinnamon and spices. 3. Roman poet Ovid suggested a proactive solution in his 'Art of Love': avoid carrying goats under your arms. 4. The FDA classifies antiperspirants as drugs because they affect the body's natural functions. 5. EverDry, the first modern antiperspirant, was introduced in 1903 but was highly acidic. 6. Modern antiperspirants can damage clothing due to aluminum chloride. 7. In San Luis Obispo County, California, having offensive body odor in libraries is illegal. 8. There's no conclusive evidence that antiperspirants cause degenerative diseases. 9. Aoki, a Japanese menswear company, developed a 'deodorant suit' to absorb sweat. 10. 'Fuwarinka' scented gum releases 'Fresh Citrus' or 'Fruity Rose' aromas from the skin for up to 6 hours. 11. Kurt Cobain was unaware 'Teen Spirit' was a deodorant brand when writing Nirvana's 'Smells Like Teen Spirit'. 12. After Matthew McConaughey revealed he doesn't use deodorant, he received a year's supply from Axe.

FDA将抗汗剂归类为药物，因为它们影响身体的自然功能。 5. 1903年，第一款现代抗汗剂EverDry推出，但它的酸性很强。 6. 现代抗汗剂中的氯化铝会损坏衣服。 7. 在加利福尼亚州圣路易斯奥比斯波县，图书馆内有难闻的体味是违法的。 8. 目前没有确凿的证据表明抗汗剂会导致退行性疾病。 9. 日本男装公司Aoki开发了一种“除臭西装”，可以吸收汗液。 10. “Fuwarinka”香糖可以让皮肤释放出“清新柑橘”或“果香玫瑰”的香气，持续6小时。 11. 库尔特·科本在创作涅槃乐队的《Smells Like Teen Spirit》时并不知道“Teen Spirit”是一个除臭剂品牌。 12. 马修·麦康纳透露他不使用除臭剂后，收到了Axe公司一年的除臭剂供应。

article_content: London (CNN) -- Two former personal assistants to celebrity chef Nigella Lawson and her ex-husband Charles Saatchi are accused of misusing company credit cards for luxury goods, a court heard on Thursday. Rahul Gajjar, an accountant for Saatchi, testified that in June 2012, Francesca had £64,336.97 in expenses, including purchases from designer labels. article_content: David Cameron tells Ukraine's president that London will support Kyiv for 'however long it takes'. The UK's newly appointed foreign secretary, David Cameron, visited Ukraine to underline British support amid its ongoing war with Russia. Cameron, the former prime minister, made his first working trip abroad as Britain's top diplomat, telling Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that the UK would support Ukraine for 'however long it takes'. 'I wanted this to be my first visit,' Cameron said, 'I admire the strength and determination of the Ukrainian people.' He was named foreign secretary on Monday. Zelenskyy said he was grateful for Cameron's gesture amid Israel's war in Gaza, which has diverted attention from Ukraine's 21st month of battle with Russia. 'The world is not so focused on the battlefield situation in Ukraine, and this dividing of the focus really does not help,' Zelenskyy said. The UK has been a close ally of Ukraine, and Cameron said Britain would continue to provide moral, diplomatic, and military support. 'We will continue to give you the moral support, the diplomatic support... but above all the military support that you need, however long it takes,' Cameron said. The UK would work with its allies 'to make sure the attention is here in Ukraine'. Ukraine's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Cameron engaged in talks on armaments and Black Sea security in Kyiv. As of last month, the UK was second to the US in providing military funds to Ukraine, giving 4.6 billion pounds ($5.7bn) in assistance and training 30,000 Ukrainian soldiers.

article_content: Japan is set to 'reopen discussions' on the international ban on whale hunting at the IWC conference in Brazil. Japan's proposal suggests that 'some scientific evidence' supports the sustainable harvesting of certain whale species. The move is backed by Iceland and Norway but faces 'strong opposition' from Australia, Brazil, and the EU. Japan accuses the IWC of 'not representing all stakeholders' in its decision-making process. Whale meat has been a 'long-standing part' of Japanese cuisine. Despite a 1982 ban, Japan, Norway, and Iceland continued whaling under the 'guise of research'. A 2014 International Court of Justice ruling found Japan's whaling 'partially justified' but not entirely. Japan now seeks to establish a Sustainable Whaling Committee for commercial whaling. article_content: By Lucy Thackray. Actress Rachel Griffiths has revealed her opinions about the struggles Australian women face in government and society as she prepares to play former Prime Minister Julia Gillard. 'We need more women on top and our girls need more strong role models,' she told Sunday Style. '(My daughter) Adelaide said to me the other day, 'Why do they only show boys' sports on television? It's so annoying!' And that's out of the mouth of an eight-year-old!' The upcoming telemovie 'Stalking Julia' is in pre-production and is based on Kerry-Anne Walsh's book 'The Stalking of Julia Gillard: How the Media and Team Rudd Brought Down the Prime Minister'. Ms Griffiths will play Australia's first female Prime Minister during her controversial three years in office. Rachel Griffiths says she was shocked by a recent survey revealing Australia is 'well down' on the list of countries for working women, though the specific survey is not named. Two years ago, Griffiths, her husband, and their three young children returned to live in Melbourne after around a decade in the US. Griffiths states that the statistics prove Australia's treatment of women is worse than in many other countries. 'I read an extraordinary survey that showed Australia was well down the list of best places to be a working woman. It's based on pay, promotion, family-friendly policies, and some areas still being culturally anti-female,' she told Sunday Style. She says the conditions are too difficult for most women to enter Australian politics. 'I get cross that some very talented women I know who would have been brilliant in office have been approached and are consciously saying no.' Griffiths, who will play former Prime Minister Julia Gillard in 'Stalking Julia', says parliament is not where 'any smart, successful woman I know really chooses to go and make a difference'. Griffiths has never been afraid to make her political beliefs known. In March this year, she appeared on ABC's Q&A and said that parliament is 'not where any smart, successful woman I know really chooses to go and make a difference'. Griffiths was arrested in 1997 for protesting the opening of the Crown Casino in Melbourne. At the time, Rachel Griffiths said that the Victorian government, led by Premier Jeff Kennett, had 'succeeded in raping our state of its dignity, compassion, and sense of community.' When asked why she protested in this manner, she said 'if I didn't flash my tits, you wouldn't have put me in the papers'. The 44-year-old Aussie actress is currently starring in Channel Nine's 'House Husbands' and is in a campaign for Sportscraft. She and her family, including her two daughters, Adelaide and Clementine, and her son, Banjo, are here to stay.
